comment: Deterministic regression scenarios for run-regression.js. Each runs under the shared determinism policy (governor off, test resolution, gate off, fluid material, seeded RNG, frozen clock). Action vocabulary: slider/checkbox/select/preset/material/stroke/pointerStroke/key/step/clear/snapshot/eval/glcheck. Grow this list one scenario per feature system — the features inventory (inventory/features.json) lists the activation recipes. A scenario may also carry "glErrors": true to run the harness's gl.getError() sweep for that scenario alone (--gl-errors on the driver turns it on for all of them).
settleComment: SETTLE WINDOWS ARE CAPPED AT 20 FRAMES POST-STROKE, on purpose. GUIDANCE §4 measured cross-boot bit-identity holding through frame 20 and breaking at frames ~20-40 (residual B, suspected real-clock timers firing at phase-random pump indices), and names shortening the settle windows as the pragmatic mitigation until residuals A and B are actually fixed. Every scenario below that used to settle 40-60 frames now settles 20; the cost is that fields are measured less settled, which is the trade GUIDANCE describes. The single deliberate exception is hotkey-freeze-toggle/still-frozen — see its comment. Restoring the long windows is a one-line-per-scenario change once residual B is closed.
invariantComment: invariants[] are relations that must hold WITHIN one run, checked by run-regression.js against the run itself (not the goldens), in compare mode AND under --record. Each names two checkpoints as left/right and asserts per field: "equal" (hashes must match; if they differ the field's scalars are consulted and the result is NEAR inside tolerance, FAIL outside) or "differ" (hashes must not match). Fields: dye, vel, display. `note` is printed whenever the invariant does not hold.

scenarios.name: plain-stroke
scenarios.comment: The canonical baseline: one seeded stroke, advected 20 frames. This is also the physics reference the kaleido-is-display-only invariant compares against, so its stroke and step count must stay identical to kaleido-display's.

scenarios.name: pointer-stroke
scenarios.comment: Same idea through the REAL input pipeline (05d handlers, brush engine spacing) — catches input-path regressions the splat path cannot. WARNING, measured 2026-08-26 across every run in results/: this scenario is the one that does not repeat. Two runs in the SAME boot have come back 155% apart on coverage and 123% apart on meanLum (08-23 09-33 vs 09-35), and its velocity hash moves run-to-run where the other nine checkpoints' hold. That is a different failure from the GUIDANCE §4 residuals — those move hashes while scalars agree to 5 decimals; this moves the deposit itself, so the settle cap does nothing for it. Read as bimodal: the stroke sometimes lands and sometimes largely does not. Likeliest suspect is the pointerdown/first-move race against the interleaved step(1) in harness.pointerStroke, or brush-engine spacing state surviving between scenarios. Until it is diagnosed, treat a pointer-stroke delta as uninformative rather than as a regression, and do NOT widen the global tolerances to accommodate it.

scenarios.name: materials
scenarios.comment: One stroke per material. setMode must follow any snapshot apply, never precede it (material-vs-snapshot ordering, 29-material-modes). 20-frame settles: clay and acrylic differ from fluid in the first frames (viscosity/plasticity act on deposit), so the shortened window still separates them — the goldens show acrylic and clay 10% apart on coverage at 50 frames and the mechanisms that produce that gap are all early.

scenarios.name: builtin-presets
scenarios.comment: Two contrast-extreme built-ins over the same stroke. Presets are parameter sets applied before the stroke, so what this probes — did applyPreset land, and does the sim respond to it — is fully visible at 20 frames.

scenarios.name: multi-arm-radial
scenarios.comment: Six-arm radial symmetry through the splat multiplier. The rosette is geometry laid down AT deposit, not something the sim has to develop, so 20 frames is if anything a cleaner read of it. Note this checkpoint is one of the two whose scalars wobble run-to-run even in one boot (|Δcoverage| up to 0.28%, |Δlum| 0.04%) — well inside tolerance, but it is why the tolerance is not set tighter.

scenarios.name: collider-lattice
scenarios.comment: Procedural obstacle field, stroke driven through it. setProcedural flips collision on itself; the reset between scenarios clears it via the next scenario's clear (obstacle texture wipe is in the features inventory if this ever leaks). The 8 pre-stroke frames stay — they exist to let the obstacle texture take effect BEFORE the dye arrives, and cutting them would test nothing. The post-stroke settle drops 60 → 20: the obstacle mask deflects flow from the first advected frame, so this now measures early wakes rather than developed ones. If a future collision bug turns out to need the long tail to show itself, this is the scenario to exempt from the cap first.

scenarios.name: kaleido-display
scenarios.comment: Kaleidoscope is display-chain: sim hashes should MATCH plain-stroke's physics under identical input while the display hash differs. That sentence is now the kaleido-is-display-only invariant below instead of a comment nothing read — which is why the stroke and the 20-frame settle here must stay bit-for-bit identical to plain-stroke's. First-enable side effect: the kaleido toggle bootstraps multiplier to 8 — pinned back to 1 here explicitly.

scenarios.name: hotkey-freeze-toggle
scenarios.comment: Space transport. The pre-freeze settle drops 20 → 10 so the 'frozen' checkpoint lands at 12 frames post-stroke, inside the stable window. The 30 post-freeze frames are DELIBERATELY kept even though that puts 'still-frozen' at 42 frames post-stroke, outside it: that checkpoint exists only to be compared against 'frozen' WITHIN this run, where residuals A and B (a same-boot ratchet and a cross-boot drift) do not apply. Shortening it would also blunt the assertion — the drift it is meant to detect is ~2% of coverage over 30 frames, so at 8 frames it would read as ~0.5% and land inside tolerance as a NEAR, hiding the very thing the checkpoint is for. 2026-09-12: two more checkpoints, 'braked' (92 frames after Space — the 0.9/frame velocity brake is down to ~0.01% of its start) and 'held' 30 frames later. Those are the pair freeze-halts-the-sim compares now that Space stands vorticity confinement and the Gravity pad down (05j): 'frozen' → 'still-frozen' is the stroke's own momentum braking out, which is the design, and only the post-brake pair says whether anything ELSE is still moving the paint.

scenarios.name: hotkey-freeze-gravity
scenarios.comment: Space with the Gravity Direction pad aimed straight down (config.AMBIENT_FORCE plus a unit SCREEN-space vector — the same keys the pad writes in 20-mixer-layout; the 05j pass flips y). The ambient force is dye-weighted and never decays on its own, so it is the one force the freeze brake could never outlast: before 2026-09-12 a frozen painting kept sinking for as long as the freeze held. Same checkpoint shape as hotkey-freeze-toggle, and the invariant reads the same post-brake pair. AMBIENT_FORCE is not registry-covered, so setup() would not reset it — the last action switches gravity off again so it cannot leak into the next scenario.

scenarios.name: hotkey-freeze-swirl
scenarios.comment: Space with Swirl (vorticity confinement, config.CURL) at the top of its slider. Confinement adds velocity in proportion to the curl already there, so at the default 25 it dies with the brake and the plain freeze scenario barely sees it; at 60 it has the most it can feed on. Same checkpoint shape as hotkey-freeze-toggle; curl is registry-covered, so setup() puts it back for the next scenario.

invariants.name: kaleido-is-display-only
invariants.why: Kaleidoscope renders in the display chain and must never touch density or velocity. Identical seed, identical stroke, identical settle — so the sim hashes must be the same field and only the rendered canvas may differ. This is also the cheapest standing detector for bug #2 (GUIDANCE §6): a display pass leaking into the sim shows up here first.
invariants.note: Expect dye NEAR, not PASS, until bug #2 is fixed. The committed goldens (2026-08-21) already show it half-broken: kaleido's vel hash IS plain-stroke's (4e6e81ea both) but its dye hash is not (d9b4a359 vs da8d052b) while coverage is identical to all five recorded decimals (0.27567 both) — a bit-level leak with no measurable magnitude, exactly the signature of the Ridges display→sim coupling. A jump from NEAR to FAIL here means the leak grew teeth.

invariants.name: freeze-halts-the-sim
invariants.why: Space is the stop key: once its velocity brake has run out, nothing may keep moving the paint. Until 2026-09-12 two of the fluid's own forces did — vorticity confinement fed on the curl that was still braking out, and the Gravity pad re-pushed the dye every step — so a frozen painting went on spreading and brightening for as long as the freeze held. 05j now skips both passes while window.__fluidFrozen is up; the projection, the brake and the splat path stay live so painting on a frozen canvas is unchanged.
invariants.assertComment: Compared AFTER the brake, not right after the keypress. Freeze is a brake, not a hard stop — toggleFreeze (04b) sets VELOCITY_DISSIPATION 0.9 and the stroke's momentum runs out over the next second — so 'frozen' → 'still-frozen' legitimately moves: velMean falls ~94% over those 30 frames and the stroke's open ends carry some dye off the canvas as they settle. By 'braked' (92 frames after Space) the residual is 0.9^92 ≈ 0.006% of its start and its mean speed sits under velMean's 0.001 absolute tolerance, so the brake's own tail no longer registers; from there to 'held' the field has to sit still to the scalar tolerances. Expect NEAR rather than PASS: the residual is geometric, never exactly zero, so the hashes move by a bit while every scalar stays inside tolerance.
invariants.note: MEASURED 2026-09-12 in one Electron boot, pre-fix vs fix. Pre-fix (HEAD 05j, Swirl at its default 25, no gravity) over the SAME braked → held window: coverage +0.04%, dye mean −0.56%, mean luminance +0.05%, velMean 0.00578 → 0.00584 — the velocity had stopped braking out and sat on a confinement-fed plateau (NEAR on the scalars, but the paint was still creeping). With the gate: coverage and dye mean identical to five decimals (0.28709 / 0.34683), display hash identical, velMean 0.00015 → 0.00001. If this FAILS again, something new is adding velocity or dye while frozen — look for a pass in the 05j sub-step loop that does not read _frozen (window.__fluidFrozen), or a splat caller that fires with no pointer down. Do not silence it by loosening the tolerance.

invariants.name: freeze-stops-gravity
invariants.why: Same contract with the Gravity Direction pad aimed down. The ambient-force pass (05j, ambientForceFrag) is dye-weighted and never runs dry, so it is the one force the brake could never outlast: with it live a frozen painting sank for as long as the freeze held.
invariants.note: MEASURED 2026-09-12 in one Electron boot, pre-fix vs fix, braked → held with the pad straight down: pre-fix coverage 0.32698 → 0.37608 (+15.0%), mean luminance +15.4%, dye mean +2.15%, velMean held at ~0.086 — FAIL, the sink never stops; with the gate coverage and dye mean identical to five decimals (0.28586 / 0.35304), display hash identical, velMean 0.00007 → 0. Expect NEAR (see freeze-halts-the-sim). A FAIL here with freeze-halts-the-sim passing means the gravity gate specifically regressed — the ambient pass in 05j must stay behind !_frozen.

invariants.name: freeze-stops-swirl
invariants.why: Same contract with vorticity confinement at its maximum. Confinement is the other force the fluid applies to itself with no hand on the canvas; while frozen it must not be allowed to feed on the curl that is still braking out.
invariants.note: MEASURED 2026-09-12 in one Electron boot, pre-fix vs fix, braked → held at Swirl 60: pre-fix coverage +0.01%, dye mean −0.44%, mean luminance +0.16%, velMean 0.00697 → 0.00803 (+15%) — the residual was GROWING, a swirl feeding on itself against the brake (NEAR on the scalars, moving forever); with the gate coverage and dye mean identical to five decimals (0.28730 / 0.35266), display hash identical, velMean 0.00016 → 0.00001. Expect NEAR (see freeze-halts-the-sim). A FAIL here with freeze-halts-the-sim passing means the confinement gate specifically regressed — the curl and vorticity passes in 05j must stay behind !_frozen.
